status: proposed real experiment; no measurements collected
objective: Distinguish elastic/damped response, delayed recovery and pre-existing rest shape in an intact fruit truss.

instrumentation.force: Measure actual cup force; select resolution and range from a pilot. Record calibration, noise and saturation rather than treating simulator limits as safe biological loads.
instrumentation.position: Measure actual tool displacement and rotation, not only motor command. Calibrate actuator compliance and backlash separately.
instrumentation.vision: Synchronized calibrated views of crown/common branch, stalk tip, calyx, berry orientation and neighboring fruit, with visible scale and tracked occlusions.
instrumentation.timing: Synchronize video and force timestamps. Select sampling bandwidth from the fastest resolved response and measure filtering delay. Keep raw data.

sequence: Record an untouched baseline long enough to characterize drift and sensor noise.
Ramp a small support displacement with the fruit attached; use a pilot to establish a reversible range.
Hold at several actual displacements and durations. The simulated 1 and 12 second holds are candidate interventions, not validated specimen settings.
Withdraw completely and observe for minutes; extend recording if response persists.
Repeat low-amplitude cycles with adequate recovery and an untouched comparison specimen.
Use independent controlled unloading or longitudinal growth observations to constrain reference curvature. Keep destructive tests separate.
analysis: Check mass/force balance, contact location, instrument drift and baseline motion before fitting material parameters.
Fit candidate models jointly to force and geometry over time, including instrument compliance and measurement uncertainty.
Report parameter tradeoffs and models that observations cannot distinguish.
Reserve whole plants and distinct amplitudes/hold durations for evaluation; do not split adjacent frames across fitting and validation.
Compare prediction errors at task-relevant contact forces and motion scales; add material complexity only when it improves held-out predictions.
exclusions: No transfer of petiole, wood, electrical-relaxation or cutting-failure parameters to fruit-stalk recovery without supporting evidence.
No permanent-set conclusion from a short residual-motion window.
No use of the rigid-fruit model to establish bruising thresholds.
